symbols.name: \(u\)
symbols.def: Generic nonnegative vector indexed by \(\mathcal J\).

symbols.name: \(H_0\)
symbols.def: Fixed sufficiently large universal numerical constant in the pilot rectangles.

symbols.name: \(\kappa\)
symbols.def: Fixed sufficiently small universal numerical constant.

symbols.name: \(D_0\)
symbols.def: Fixed universal cutoff separating the bounded-alphabet fallback from the Jackson branch.

symbols.name: \(J_{K_d}\)
symbols.def: One-dimensional order-four Jackson kernel constructed in \(\mathrm{def:jackson-kernel}\).

symbols.name: \(B_i\)
symbols.def: Independent fair mark for an included observation, with zero denoting pilot and one denoting evaluation.

symbols.name: \(N'_{\jmath,x}\)
symbols.def: Count in confounder cell \(x\) and coordinate \(\jmath\) among included observations with mark \(B_i=0\).

symbols.name: \(N_{\jmath,x}\)
symbols.def: Count in confounder cell \(x\) and coordinate \(\jmath\) among included observations with mark \(B_i=1\).

symbols.name: \(P_{x,K_d}\)
symbols.space: real polynomials of coordinate degree at most \(2(K_d-1)\)
symbols.def: Polynomial obtained by convolving \(\bar f_\epsilon\) on \(Q_x\) with the product Jackson kernel.

symbols.name: \(U_h(N;z)\)
symbols.def: Centered factorial lift of the monomial \((q-z)^h\), constructed in \(\mathrm{def:jackson-factorial-estimator}\).

symbols.name: \(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}\)
symbols.def: Pilot-local centered-factorial lift of \(P_{x,K_d}\), clipped at its local stochastic scale.

symbols.name: \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}\)
symbols.def: Bounded-alphabet empirical cellwise-ratio statistic constructed in \(\mathrm{def:empirical-ratio-estimator}\).

symbols.name: \(c_\epsilon\)
symbols.def: Positive constant depending only on \(\epsilon\) asserted by the minimax theorem.

symbols.name: \(C_\epsilon\)
symbols.def: Finite constant depending only on \(\epsilon\) asserted by the minimax theorem.

symbols.name: \(\mathbf P\)
symbols.def: First probability vector in the normalized two-sample distance experiment.

symbols.name: \(\mathbf Q\)
symbols.def: Second probability vector in the normalized two-sample distance experiment.

symbols.name: \(\theta\)
symbols.def: Vector \(\theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_d)\) indexing the equal-mass dense hard submodel.

symbols.name: \(\lambda_{n,d}\)
symbols.type: Poissonized expected count per confounder cell

symbols.name: \(r\)
symbols.def: Generic order in the exponential likelihood expansion.

symbols.name: \(L_{\theta_x}\)
symbols.def: Likelihood ratio at contrast \(\theta_x\) relative to contrast zero in a Poissonized cell with expected count \(\lambda_{n,d}\).

symbols.name: \(\nu_{0,K}\)
symbols.def: First measure obtained from a symmetrized norming measure for \(E_K\).

symbols.name: \(\nu_{1,K}\)
symbols.def: Second measure obtained from the same symmetrized norming measure for \(E_K\).

symbols.name: \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\)
symbols.type: first symmetric product prior on dense contrasts
symbols.def: Product prior obtained by scaling \(\nu_{0,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\) by \(a_{n,d}\).

symbols.name: \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\)
symbols.type: second symmetric product prior on dense contrasts
symbols.def: Product prior obtained by scaling \(\nu_{1,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\) by \(a_{n,d}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathbb M_{0,n,d}\)
symbols.space: probability laws on finite causal samples
symbols.def: Observation law obtained by mixing a \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\)-sample from \(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) under \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathbb M_{1,n,d}\)
symbols.space: probability laws on finite causal samples
symbols.def: Observation law obtained by mixing a \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\)-sample from \(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) under \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}\)
symbols.def: Minimax risk for the same class and target when the sample size is independent \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\).

assumptions.condition: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent draws from the observed \((X,A,Y)\)-margin of \(P\).

definitions.name: published unrestricted discrete-confounder causal law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}:=\{P: P\text{ is a law of }(X,A,Y,Y(0),Y(1))\text{ with }X\in[d],\ A,Y,Y(0),Y(1)\in\{0,1\},\text{ and }P\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:conditional-exchangeability},\mathrm{ass:fixed-overlap}\}\) for every \(d\geq2\) and \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).

definitions.name: four-cell overlap cone
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_\epsilon:=\{u\in\mathbb R_+^4:\epsilon s(u)\leq s_1(u)\leq(1-\epsilon)s(u)\}\), where \(s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1}\) and \(s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u)\).

definitions.name: globally Lipschitz observational cell-value extension
definitions.construction: For \(u\in\mathbb R_+^4\) with \(s(u)>0\), define \(g_{a,\epsilon}(u):=s(u)u_{a1}/\max\{s_a(u),\epsilon s(u)\}\) and \(\bar f_\epsilon(u):=\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}g_{a,\epsilon}(u)\); set \(g_{a,\epsilon}(0)=\bar f_\epsilon(0)=0\).

definitions.name: bounded-alphabet empirical-ratio fallback
definitions.construction: Let \(\overline N_x=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x\}\), \(\overline N_{ax}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a\}\), and \(\overline S_{ax}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a,Y_i=1\}\). Put \(\widehat p_x=\overline N_x/n\), \(\widehat\mu_{ax}=\overline S_{ax}/\overline N_{ax}\) with \(0/0=0\), and \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}=\sum_{x=1}^d\widehat p_x\max_a\widehat\mu_{ax}\).

definitions.name: positive order-four tensor Jackson approximation
definitions.construction: For integer \(K_d\geq2\), let \(J_{K_d}(t)=c_{K_d}[\sin(K_dt/2)/\sin(t/2)]^4\) on \([-\pi,\pi]\), with removable values filled continuously and \(c_{K_d}\) chosen so that \(\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}J_{K_d}(t)\,dt=1\). For a rectangle \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) with center \(b_{\jmath,x}=(\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x})/2\) and radius \(r_{\jmath,x}=(u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x})/2\), define \(P_{x,K_d}\) by the even product convolution \(P_{x,K_d}(b_x+r_x\odot\cos\theta)=\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^4}\bar f_\epsilon(b_x+r_x\odot\cos(\theta+t))\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}J_{K_d}(t_{\jmath})\,dt\).

definitions.name: explicit all-data pilot-local Jackson--factorial estimator
definitions.construction: Put \(L_d=\log(ed)\), \(m=n/8\), and \(K_d=\max\{2,\lfloor\kappa L_d\rfloor\}\). If \(d<D_0\), return \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}\); if \(d\geq D_0\) and \(n<d/L_d\), return \(1/2\). Otherwise draw \(M\sim\operatorname{Pois}(n/4)\), and on \(M\leq n\) mark the first \(M\) observations independently by \(B_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), producing independent pilot and evaluation counts \(N'_{\jmath,x}\) and \(N_{\jmath,x}\); on \(M>n\), set the randomized output to zero. For \(M\leq n\), let \(c_{\jmath,x}=N'_{\jmath,x}/m\), \(h_{\jmath,x}=H_0\{\sqrt{c_{\jmath,x}L_d/m}+L_d/m\}\), \(\ell_{\jmath,x}=\max\{0,c_{\jmath,x}-h_{\jmath,x}\}\), \(u_{\jmath,x}=c_{\jmath,x}+h_{\jmath,x}\), and \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\), with center \(b_x\) and coordinate radii \(r_x\). Expand \(P_{x,K_d}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)=\sum_\alpha b_{x,\alpha}((v-b_x)/r_x)^\alpha\). Define \(U_h(N;z)=\sum_{t=0}^h\binom ht(-z)^{h-t}(N)_t/m^t\), \(S_x=(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath}r_{\jmath,x}\), \(Z_x=\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)+\sum_\alpha b_{x,\alpha}\prod_{\jmath}U_{\alpha_{\jmath}}(N_{\jmath,x};b_{\jmath,x})/r_{\jmath,x}^{\alpha_{\jmath}}\), and \(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}=\Pi_{[\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)-d^{1/4}S_x,\,\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)+d^{1/4}S_x]}(Z_x)\). The randomized statistic is \(\widetilde V=\Pi_{[0,1]}(\sum_xT_x^{\mathrm{JF}})\). In the Jackson branch define the all-data estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}:=E[\widetilde V\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n]\), where the conditional expectation integrates only the displayed auxiliary Poisson count and marks.

definitions.name: minimax oracle-value mean-squared error
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}:=\inf_{\widehat V}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}}E_P[(\widehat V(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-V^\star(P))^2]\), where the infimum is over all measurable estimators.

definitions.name: equal-propensity normalized \(L_1\) subexperiment
definitions.construction: For \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\), set \(q_{11,x}=q_{00,x}=P_x/4\) and \(q_{10,x}=q_{01,x}=Q_x/4\), and complete the observed law with conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes, treatment propensity \(1/2\), and consistency.

definitions.name: equal-mass dense sign experiment and its symmetric fuzzy hypotheses
definitions.construction:
For \(	heta\in[-1/2,1/2]^d\), define \(P_	heta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) by \(p_x=1/d\), \(\pi_x=1/2\), \(\mu_{1x}=(1+	heta_x)/2\), and \(\mu_{0x}=(1-	heta_x)/2\). Complete the observed law by drawing \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with these means, drawing \(A\mid X=x\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently of the potential outcomes, and setting \(Y=Y(A)\). For even \(K\), let \(E_K=\inf_{p:\deg(p)\leq K}\sup_{t\in[-1,1]}\lvert\lvert tvert-p(t)vert\), and obtain symmetric probability measures \(
u_{0,K}\) and \(
u_{1,K}\) by taking the negative and positive parts of twice a symmetrized norm-one Hahn--Banach measure that annihilates every polynomial of degree at most \(K\) and integrates \(\lvert tvert\) to \(E_K\). Thus their moments agree through degree \(K\) and \(\int\lvert tvert\,d
u_{1,K}-\int\lvert tvert\,d
u_{0,K}=2E_K\). Put \(K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}=2\lceil4L_dceil\), \(\lambda_{n,d}=2n/d\), and \(a_{n,d}=\sqrt{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}/(64\lambda_{n,d})}\). Let \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\) be the pushforward of \(
u_{0,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\) under the coordinatewise scaling map \(t\mapsto a_{n,d}t\), and define \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\) analogously from \(
u_{1,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\). Let \(\mathbb M_{0,n,d}\) and \(\mathbb M_{1,n,d}\) be the respective observation mixtures when the total sample size is independent \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\). Finally, define \(\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}:=\inf_{\widehat V}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}}E_P[(\widehat V-V^\star(P))^2]\) in that Poissonized experiment and \(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}:=E_{\Pi_{1,n,d}}V^\star(P_	heta^{\mathrm{dense}})-E_{\Pi_{0,n,d}}V^\star(P_	heta^{\mathrm{dense}})\).

definitions.name: overlap-cone approximation--moment dual handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathscr H_\epsilon^{\mathrm{const}}\) is the route that rescales the pilot-local four-cell rectangles by their Poisson noise geometry, optimizes the tensor-polynomial bias--variance functional for \(\bar f_\epsilon\), and dualizes the approximation constraint into overlap-preserving moment-matched priors for the target \(V^\star(P)\).

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\), consistency, conditional exchangeability, and fixed overlap identify \(V^\star(P)=\sum_{x=1}^dp_x\max\{\mu_{0x},\mu_{1x}\}\). Moreover, \(q_x\in\mathcal C_\epsilon\), \(\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)=p_x\max\{\mu_{0x},\mu_{1x}\}\), \(0\leq\bar f_\epsilon(u)\leq s(u)\), and \(\lvert\bar f_\epsilon(u)-\bar f_\epsilon(v)\rvert\leq(1+\epsilon^{-1})\lVert u-v\rVert_1\) for all \(u,v\in\mathbb R_+^4\).
statements.justification: The extension removes empirical off-cone denominators before approximation and makes null cells and overlap-boundary cells part of one analytic object.
statements.gap: LuedtkeVanderLaan2016OptimalValue identifies the scalar value and its local regularity boundary, while ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete uses the same observed cells for linear means; neither gives this global four-cell Lipschitz extension.
statements.consumer: The Jackson construction can approximate one globally controlled function on every pilot rectangle instead of solving a different constrained ratio problem cell by cell.

statements.statement: Let \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) have center \(b_x\) and positive radii \(r_{\jmath,x}\). The single polynomial \(P_{x,K_d}\) in \(\mathrm{def:jackson-kernel}\) has coordinate degree \(2(K_d-1)\) and satisfies, for every \(v\in Q_x\), \(\lvert P_{x,K_d}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(v)\rvert\leq C_\epsilon\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\{\sqrt{(v_{\jmath}-\ell_{\jmath,x})(u_{\jmath,x}-v_{\jmath})}/K_d+r_{\jmath,x}/K_d^2\}\). If \(P_{x,K_d}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)=\sum_\alpha b_{x,\alpha}((v-b_x)/r_x)^\alpha\), then \(\sum_\alpha\lvert b_{x,\alpha}\rvert\leq A^{K_d}(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath}r_{\jmath,x}\) for a universal \(A<\infty\). Both bounds hold for the same polynomial when \(Q_x\) touches the origin, a coordinate face, or a treatment-effect tie surface.
statements.justification: This is the exact certificate the parent could not supply: pointwise vertex adaptation and the centered coefficient envelope are properties of one explicit polynomial.
statements.gap: JiaoHanWeissman2018L1 localizes a two-dimensional absolute difference and CaiLow2011L1 controls scalar absolute-value approximation; neither proves the joint four-dimensional observational-ratio certificate.
statements.consumer: The centered factorial lift uses the coefficient envelope while the global bias calculation uses the pointwise bound, so this lemma connects both halves of the estimator proof.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(B=1+\epsilon^{-1}\), which is a Lipschitz constant for \(\bar f_\epsilon\) by \(\mathrm{prop:identification-and-extension}\).  Suppress the cell subscript and write \(Q=\prod_{j=1}^4[\ell_j,u_j]\), \(b_j=(\ell_j+u_j)/2\), and \(r_j=(u_j-\ell_j)/2>0\).  For \(K=K_d\), define
\[
 H(\vartheta)=\bar f_\epsilon(b+r\odot\cos\vartheta),
 \qquad
 \mathcal J_KH(\vartheta)=\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^4}H(\vartheta+t)\prod_{j=1}^4J_K(t_j)\,dt.
\]
This is exactly the construction in \(\mathrm{def:jackson-kernel}\).

The elementary inequalities
\[
 \left|\frac{\sin(Kt/2)}{\sin(t/2)}\right|
 \leq C\min\{K,|t|^{-1}\},
 \qquad |t|\leq\pi,
\]
and the reverse bound on \(|t|\leq K^{-1}\) show that the unnormalized fourth power has integral between constant multiples of \(K^3\).  Hence its normalized version obeys
\[
 0\leq J_K(t)\leq\frac{CK}{(1+K|t|)^4},\qquad
 \int|t|J_K(t)\,dt\leq\frac CK,\qquad
 \int t^2J_K(t)\,dt\leq\frac C{K^2}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
The fourth power is an even trigonometric polynomial of degree \(2(K-1)\).  Convolution therefore makes \(\mathcal J_KH\) an even trigonometric polynomial, separately in each coordinate, of coordinate degree at most \(2(K-1)\).  Since an even trigonometric polynomial of degree \(D\) is a polynomial of degree \(D\) in \(\cos\vartheta\), this defines the polynomial \(P_{x,K_d}\) in the statement with the asserted coordinate degree.

If \(v=b+r\odot\cos\vartheta\), Taylor's formula for cosine with second derivative bounded by one gives
\[
 r_j|\cos(\vartheta_j+t_j)-\cos\vartheta_j|
 \leq r_j|\sin\vartheta_j|\,|t_j|+\frac12r_jt_j^2.
\]
Moreover
\[
 r_j|\sin\vartheta_j|=\sqrt{(v_j-\ell_j)(u_j-v_j)}.
\]
Apply the \(B\)-Lipschitz inequality to the integrand, integrate with (1), and sum over the four coordinates.  This proves
\[
 |P_{x,K_d}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(v)|
 \leq C_\epsilon\sum_{j=1}^4\left\{
 \frac{\sqrt{(v_j-\ell_j)(u_j-v_j)}}{K_d}+\frac{r_j}{K_d^2}
 \right\}.                                                               \tag{2}
\]

For the coefficient assertion, positivity and normalization of the product kernel imply
\[
 \sup_{v\in Q}|P_{x,K_d}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b)|
 \leq B\sum_{j=1}^4r_j=:S.                                               \tag{3}
\]
Expand the left side of (3) in the tensor Chebyshev basis on \([-1,1]^4\).  The cosine integral formula bounds each tensor Chebyshev coefficient by \(16S\).  If \(c_h\) denotes the sum of the absolute monomial coefficients of the Chebyshev polynomial \(T_h\), then \(T_{h+1}=2zT_h-T_{h-1}\) gives
\[
 c_{h+1}\leq2c_h+c_{h-1},\qquad c_0=c_1=1,\qquad
 c_h\leq(1+\sqrt2)^h.
\]
Writing \(D=2(K_d-1)\), multiplying the four one-dimensional bounds and summing over at most \((D+1)^4\) tensor coefficients gives
\[
 \sum_\alpha|b_{x,\alpha}|
 \leq16S(D+1)^4(1+\sqrt2)^{4D}
 \leq A^{K_d}(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}r_{\jmath,x}
\]
for a universal finite \(A\).  Equations (2) and (3) concern the same convolution polynomial.  No part of the argument requires an interior rectangle or differentiability of \(\bar f_\epsilon\), so it applies when \(Q_x\) touches the origin, a coordinate face, or a tie surface.

statements.statement: In the uncapped Poisson comparison experiment induced by \(M\) and \(B_i\), conditional on the pilot counts the statistics \(U_h(N;z)\) satisfy \(E[U_h(N;z)]=(q-z)^h\) and \(E[U_h(N;z)U_t(N;z)]=\sum_{\ell=0}^{h\wedge t}\binom h\ell\binom t\ell\ell!(q/m)^\ell(q-z)^{h+t-2\ell}\). With the pilot rectangles and clipping in \(\mathrm{def:jackson-factorial-estimator}\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\), \(\lvert E[T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}]-\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)\rvert\leq C_\epsilon\{\sqrt{p_x/(mL_d)}+1/(mL_d)\}\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}})\leq C_\epsilon d^{1/16}\{p_xL_d/m+L_d^2/m^2\}\). The contribution of pilot failure obeys these same local \(p_x\)-dependent scales.
statements.justification: The exact centered factorial identity prevents the polynomial center from reappearing in the variance, while local pilot tails prevent a dimension-only exceptional-event loss.
statements.gap: JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015Functionals and JiaoHanWeissman2018L1 use factorial moments after localization, but not with random four-coordinate ratio boxes, local clipping, and arbitrary cell masses.
statements.consumer: Summing these cell bounds yields the logarithmic upper rate without treating uncentered cell mean-squared errors as independent contributions.
statements.proof_tex:
Work first in the uncapped Poisson experiment.  Poisson thinning from \(M\sim\operatorname{Pois}(n/4)\) and the fair marks \(B_i\) gives, with \(m=n/8\), mutually independent counts
\[
 N'_{\jmath,x}\sim\operatorname{Pois}(mq_{\jmath,x}),\qquad
 N_{\jmath,x}\sim\operatorname{Pois}(mq_{\jmath,x})
\]
over all \((\jmath,x)\), with the pilot array independent of the evaluation array.  For a scalar \(N\sim\operatorname{Pois}(mq)\), the definition of \(U_h\) gives the exponential generating function
\[
 \sum_{h\geq0}U_h(N;z)\frac{w^h}{h!}=e^{-zw}(1+w/m)^N.
\]
Taking the expectation of one copy and of the product of copies at \(w,v\), respectively, gives
\[
 E e^{-zw}(1+w/m)^N=e^{(q-z)w},
\]
and
\[
 E\!\left[e^{-z(w+v)}(1+w/m)^N(1+v/m)^N\right]
 =\exp\{(q-z)(w+v)+(q/m)wv\}.
\]
Coefficient extraction proves both factorial identities in the statement.

Set \(L=L_d\), \(\tau=L/m\), \(c_\jmath=N'_{\jmath,x}/m\), and
\[
 G_x=\bigcap_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\bigl\{|c_\jmath-q_{\jmath,x}|\leq h_\jmath/4\bigr\},
 \qquad v_x=\sqrt{p_x\tau}+\tau.
\]
The following bounds are now derived from the displayed pilot construction.  On \(G_x\), \(q_x\in Q_x\), \(h_\jmath/2\leq r_\jmath\leq h_\jmath\), and solving the quadratic inequality between \(c_\jmath\) and \(q_{\jmath,x}\) yields
\[
 c_\jmath\leq C(q_{\jmath,x}+\tau),\qquad
 q_{\jmath,x}\leq C(c_\jmath+\tau).
\]
Consequently
\[
 \sum_\jmath r_\jmath\leq Cv_x,\qquad
 \frac{q_{\jmath,x}}{mr_\jmath^2}\leq\frac C L.                     \tag{4}
\]
For completeness, these conclusions also hold when \(q_{\jmath,x}=0\), because then the corresponding Poisson count is zero almost surely.

To control the complement, for \(W\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda)\), exponential Markov applied to
\(E e^{t(W-\lambda)}=\exp\{\lambda(e^t-1-t)\}\) gives, for \(z\geq1\),
\[
 \Pr\{|W-\lambda|>\sqrt{2\lambda z}+2z\}\leq2e^{-z}.                \tag{5}
\]
Choose the single numerical constant \(H_0\) large enough that the event in (5) with \(z=100L\) implies
\[
 |W/m-q|\leq\frac{H_0}{4}\left\{\sqrt{(W/m)L/m}+L/m\right\}.
\]
This follows by considering \(\lambda\geq C L\), where \(W\geq\lambda/2\), and \(\lambda<CL\), where the additive \(H_0L/m\) term dominates.  Integrating (5) above \(100L\), and using \(W/m\leq q+|W/m-q|\), proves for \(t=1,2,4\)
\[
 E\left[\left\{|W/m-q|+\sqrt{(W/m)\tau}+\tau\right\}^t
       \mathbf1_{\mathrm{bad}}\right]
 \leq C e^{-40L}(\sqrt{q\tau}+\tau)^t.                              \tag{6}
\]
Independence across the four coordinates, a union bound, and Cauchy--Schwarz with the fourth moment in (6) give
\[
 E\left[\left\{\|b_x-q_x\|_1+\sum_\jmath r_\jmath\right\}^t
       \mathbf1_{G_x^c}\right]
 \leq C e^{-20L}v_x^t,\qquad t=1,2,                                  \tag{7}
\]
and (4), together with the corresponding unconditional second moments, gives
\[
 E\left[\left(\sum_\jmath r_\jmath\right)^2\mathbf1_{G_x}\right]
 \leq Cv_x^2.                                                         \tag{8}
\]
Thus the failure cost retains the local \(p_x\)-scale.

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:simultaneous-jackson-certificate}\) on \(G_x\).  If \(\ell_\jmath=0\), then \(c_\jmath\leq h_\jmath\), whence \(c_\jmath+ h_\jmath\leq C\tau\) and
\[
 \sqrt{(q_{\jmath,x}-\ell_\jmath)(u_\jmath-q_{\jmath,x})}
 \leq C\sqrt{q_{\jmath,x}\tau},\qquad r_\jmath\leq C\tau.
\]
If \(\ell_\jmath>0\), then \(c_\jmath>h_\jmath\), so \(q_{\jmath,x}\geq3c_\jmath/4\) and \(r_\jmath\leq C\sqrt{q_{\jmath,x}\tau}\).  Since \(\sum_\jmath\sqrt{q_{\jmath,x}}\leq2\sqrt{p_x}\), the pointwise polynomial bias is
\[
 |P_{x,K_d}(q_x)-\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)|
 \leq C_\epsilon\left\{\frac{\sqrt{p_x\tau}}{K_d}+\frac{\tau}{K_d^2}\right\}. \tag{9}
\]

Conditional on the pilot, unbiasedness of the factorial lift gives \(E(Z_x\mid N')=P_{x,K_d}(q_x)\).  From the second factorial identity and (4),
\[
 \frac{E\{U_h(N;q_0)^2\}}{r^{2h}}
 \leq\sum_{\ell=0}^h\binom h\ell^2\ell!(C/L)^\ell
 \leq\exp(Ch^2/L)                                                     \tag{10}
\]
whenever \(|q-q_0|\leq r\).  Combine (10), coordinate independence, Minkowski's inequality, and the coefficient envelope from \(\mathrm{lem:simultaneous-jackson-certificate}\).  With \(S_x=(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_\jmath r_\jmath\),
\[
 E\{(Z_x-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x))^2\mid N'\}
 \leq S_x^2\exp(C_1K_d+C_2K_d^2/L).                                  \tag{11}
\]
Choose \(\kappa>0\) sufficiently small and then \(D_0\) sufficiently large.  Since \(K_d=\max\{2,\lfloor\kappa L\rfloor\}\), (11) is at most \(C S_x^2d^{1/16}\) for \(d\geq D_0\); increasing \(C\) covers the remaining finite values.

Write \(W_x=Z_x-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)\), \(t_x=d^{1/4}S_x\), and note the elementary projection inequalities
\[
 |\Pi_{[-t,t]}(w)-w|\leq w^2/t,\qquad |\Pi_{[-t,t]}(w)|\leq|w|.       \tag{12}
\]
On \(G_x\), equations (9)--(12), \(|\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)-\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)|\leq S_x\), and \(d^{-3/16}\leq C/L^2\) give
\[
 |E(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}\mid N')-\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)|
 \leq C_\epsilon\left\{\sqrt{\frac{p_x}{mL}}+\frac1{mL}\right\}, \tag{13}
\]
and
\[
 E\{(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}-\bar f_\epsilon(q_x))^2\mid N'\}
 \leq C S_x^2d^{1/16}.                                                 \tag{14}
\]
On \(G_x^c\), clipping and global Lipschitzness give the deterministic inequality
\[
 |T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}-\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)|
 \leq(1+\epsilon^{-1})\|b_x-q_x\|_1+d^{1/4}S_x.
\]
Its first two moments are controlled by (7); because \(e^{-20L}d^{1/2}\leq Cd^{1/16}\), they fit respectively into the right side of (13) and the expectation of (14).  Integrating (13)--(14) and using (8), \(v_x^2\leq2(p_xL/m+L^2/m^2)\), proves
\[
 |E T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}-\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)|
 \leq C_\epsilon\left\{\sqrt{\frac{p_x}{mL_d}}+\frac1{mL_d}\right\},
\]
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}})
 \leq C_\epsilon d^{1/16}\left\{\frac{p_xL_d}{m}+\frac{L_d^2}{m^2}\right\}.
\]
This proves the stated control, including pilot failure, null coordinates, boundary means, and ties.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is \(C_\epsilon<\infty\) such that the explicit all-data estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}\) satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}}E_P[(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}-V^\star(P))^2]\leq C_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\) for every \(n\geq1\) and \(d\geq2\). The bound permits unknown unequal propensities, arbitrary occupied-cell masses, null cells, outcome means at zero or one, and exact treatment-effect ties.
statements.justification: This named estimator and its uniform rate are the declared estimation-axis upgrade over the parent's empirical-ratio upper bound.
statements.gap: The parent certifies only \(d/n\) risk. JiaoHanWeissman2018L1 proves a logarithmic gain for normalized multinomial distance, not for unknown observational arm ratios on the full causal class.
statements.consumer: Analysts using categorical adjustment obtain a worst-case reliability benchmark showing that \(d\) comparable to \(n\) still permits consistent oracle-value estimation.

statements.statement: Every \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\) mapped by \(\mathrm{def:l1-embedding}\) yields a law in \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) with \(p_x=(P_x+Q_x)/2\), \(\pi_x=1/2\), and \(V^\star(P)=1/2+\lVert\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\rVert_1/4\). From \(n\) draws from each of \(\mathbf P\) and \(\mathbf Q\), an explicit Markov kernel produces exactly \(n\) independent causal observations, so the causal minimax risk is at least one sixteenth of the corresponding normalized two-sample \(L_1\) risk.
statements.justification: The exact reduction is the required sanity case and transfers the dense normalized-distance obstruction without replacing the full observational upper problem by its equal-propensity slice.
statements.gap: JiaoHanWeissman2018L1 studies the source experiment; it does not state causal class membership, the oracle-value identity, or the fixed-size Markov reduction.
statements.consumer: The all-estimator lower theorem uses this slice in the regime where the published normalized-distance lower bound has the correct logarithmic scale.

statements.statement: Choose the universal cutoff \(D_0\) sufficiently large. For every \(d\geq D_0\) and \(n>d^2\), the construction in \(\mathrm{def:dense-moment-matching-construction}\) has even degree \(8L_d\leq K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}<8L_d+2\), amplitude \(a_{n,d}^2=K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}d/(128n)\leq1/4\), and, for every \(\theta\in[-a_{n,d},a_{n,d}]^d\), a law \(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) satisfying \(p_x=1/d\), \(\pi_x=1/2\), \(\mu_{1x}=(1+\theta_x)/2\), \(\mu_{0x}=(1-\theta_x)/2\), and \(V^\star(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})=1/2+(2d)^{-1}\sum_{x=1}^d\lvert\theta_x\rvert\). The symmetric measures \(\nu_{0,K}\) and \(\nu_{1,K}\) exist for every even \(K\), match moments through degree \(K\), and have absolute-moment gap \(2E_K\) with \(E_K\asymp K^{-1}\). Consequently \(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}=a_{n,d}E_{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}\asymp a_{n,d}/K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}\). Writing \(\lambda_{n,d}=2n/d\), the one-cell likelihood identity under \(\theta_x=0\) is \(E_0[L_{\theta_x}L_{\theta_x'}]=\exp(\lambda_{n,d}\theta_x\theta_x')\); hence moment matching and tensorization give \[\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb M_{0,n,d},\mathbb M_{1,n,d})\leq d\left\{\sum_{r=K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}+1}^{\infty}\frac{(\lambda_{n,d}a_{n,d}^2)^r}{r!}\right\}^{1/2}\leq d\left\{\frac{(e/64)^{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}+1}}{1-e/64}\right\}^{1/2}\leq\frac1{16}.\] Under either product prior, \(\operatorname{Var}\{V^\star(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}\leq a_{n,d}^2/(4d)\), and \(D_0\) can be chosen so that \(\Pi_{0,n,d}(\lvert V^\star-E_{\Pi_{0,n,d}}V^\star\rvert>\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}/4)\leq1/8\) and \(\Pi_{1,n,d}(\lvert V^\star-E_{\Pi_{1,n,d}}V^\star\rvert>\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}/4)\leq1/8\). The two fuzzy hypotheses therefore imply \(\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}\geq c_\epsilon(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}})^2\geq c_\epsilon d/[nK_d^{\mathrm{lb}}]\). Finally, applying any fixed-sample estimator to the first \(n\) observations whenever an independent \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\) total count is at least \(n\) yields the quantified transfer \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\geq\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}-P\{\operatorname{Pois}(2n)<n\}\geq c_\epsilon d/[n\log(ed)]-e^{-n/4}\geq c_\epsilon d/[n\log(ed)]\), after decreasing \(c_\epsilon\).
statements.justification: This lemma turns the formerly named dense splice into a finite chain of membership, moment-duality, mixture-distance, concentration, and de-Poissonization inequalities.
statements.gap: CaiLow2011L1, Lemma 1 and its Hahn--Banach proof, supplies the symmetric moment-prior existence and the \(K^{-1}\) absolute-value separation; JiaoHanWeissman2018L1, the Poisson-mixture total-variation lemma in the proof of Theorem 3 and its fixed-sample comparison, supplies closely related tail and transfer templates. Neither source states this equal-mass causal sign experiment or its all-regime target scaling.
statements.consumer: The all-estimator lower theorem uses this lemma exactly in the previously uncovered range \(n>d^2\).

statements.statement: For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is \(c_\epsilon>0\) such that \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\geq c_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\) for every \(n\geq1\) and \(d\geq2\). The proof must cover all measurable estimators by splicing an overlap-preserving Poisson moment-matching experiment when \(n>d^2\), the exact normalized \(L_1\) reduction when \(d/\log(ed)\leq n\leq d^2\), and null-cell padding plus a regular two-point submodel in the saturated and bounded-alphabet regimes.
statements.justification: The lower splice certifies that the logarithmic gain is information-theoretically sharp rather than an artifact of the constructed estimator.
statements.gap: The parent lower envelope is smaller in the small-alphabet region, and JiaoHanWeissman2018L1 only covers the normalized distance regime with logarithmic sample--dimension restrictions; the dense causal sign experiment supplies the missing range.
statements.consumer: The lower bound tells users and software authors when no alternative estimation strategy can uniformly outperform the Jackson--factorial rate.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are constants \(0<c_\epsilon\leq C_\epsilon<\infty\) such that, for every \(n\geq1\) and \(d\geq2\), \(c_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\leq\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\leq\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}}E_P[(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}-V^\star(P))^2]\leq C_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\).
statements.justification: The matched frontier closes the parent's factor-logarithmic achievability gap and replaces its algebraic lower-envelope elbow by the true all-regime scale.
statements.gap: No located paper combines unrestricted discrete causal ratios, exact optimal-treatment ties, a full-class logarithmic estimator, and an all-regime converse.
statements.consumer: The frontier is directly usable as a sample-size law for scalar oracle-value reporting with high-dimensional categorical adjustment.

statements.statement: The matched frontier recovers the banked parent as a corollary on the identical class: uniformly over \(n\geq1\) and \(d\geq2\), the new upper rate is at most a constant multiple of \(d/n\), while its lower rate is at least a constant multiple of \(\min\{1,\sqrt d/n+d/[n\log(en)]\}\). For every \(2\leq d<D_0\), \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}=\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}\). Separately, for every bounded sequence of alphabets, \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}=\Theta_\epsilon(n^{-1})\).
statements.justification: This explicit corner check establishes that the run is an estimation refinement of the parent rather than a different model or estimand.
statements.gap: The parent leaves a nonmatching bracket and an unresolved consistency region; this proposition records exactly how every certified parent conclusion is retained.
statements.consumer: Downstream users of the parent bracket can substitute the matched rate without changing their causal assumptions or scalar target.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(r_{n,d}=\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\) and \(a=d/[n\log(ed)]\).  Since \(\log(ed)\geq1\), a two-case check according as \(d\geq n\) or \(d<n\) gives \(r_{n,d}\leq d/n\).  Also
\[
 \frac{\sqrt d/n}{d/[n\log(ed)]}=\frac{\log(ed)}{\sqrt d}
\]
is bounded uniformly for integers \(d\geq2\).  If \(a>1\), the parent minimum is at most one, hence at most \(r_{n,d}=1\).  Suppose \(a\leq1\).  If \(n\geq d\), then \(\log(en)\geq\log(ed)\), so
\(d/[n\log(en)]\leq a\).  If \(n<d\), put \(t=d/n>1\).  The inequality \(a\leq1\) says \(t\leq\log(ed)=\log(en)+\log t\).  For \(t\geq2\), \(\log t\leq t/2\), and hence \(t\leq2\log(en)\); the case \(1<t<2\) has the same conclusion after changing the constant.  Thus \(\log(ed)=\log(en)+\log t\leq C\log(en)\), and \(d/[n\log(en)]\leq Ca\).  Hence, for a universal \(C\),
\[
 \min\left\{1,\frac{\sqrt d}{n}+\frac d{n\log(en)}\right\}
 \leq C r_{n,d}.                                                       \tag{33}
\]
Applying \(\mathrm{thm:matched-minimax-frontier}\) to these deterministic inequalities proves both comparisons with the banked bracket on the identical class.

The equality \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}=\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}\) for \(2\leq d<D_0\) is the first branch of \(\mathrm{def:jackson-factorial-estimator}\).  Finally, along any sequence with \(2\leq d\leq D<\infty\), the quantity \(d/\log(ed)\) is bounded above and bounded away from zero.  The matched frontier therefore gives \(c_{\epsilon,D}/n\leq\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\leq C_{\epsilon,D}/n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), which is the asserted bounded-alphabet parametric conclusion.

statements.statement: Along arbitrary sequences \(n\to\infty\) with \(d=d_n\geq2\), uniform consistency for estimating \(V^\star(P)\) over \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) is possible if and only if \(d=o(n\log(en))\). Moreover, \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}=\Theta_\epsilon(n^{-1})\) if and only if \(d=O(1)\).
statements.justification: These equivalences settle the parent's intermediate consistency region and state the operational phase boundaries in invariant form.
statements.gap: The parent proves only necessity of \(d=o(n\log n)\) and sufficiency of \(d=o(n)\), while its bounded-dimensional parametric boundary is retained.
statements.consumer: A categorical-adjustment workflow can determine whether enlarging the table still permits any uniformly reliable scalar optimal-value report.

statements.statement: Along each nonsaturated sequence with \(d\to\infty\) and \(d/[n\log(ed)]\to0\), does the normalized risk \((n\log(ed)/d)\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) converge to a finite positive limit, and can an estimator attaining that limit be derived through \(\mathscr H_\epsilon^{\mathrm{const}}\)?
statements.justification: The matched rate makes a correctly normalized constant question well posed and asks whether the estimation upgrade can be sharpened from comparison constants to exact efficiency.
statements.gap: CaiLow2011L1 obtains a Bernstein-constant characterization in a Gaussian absolute-value experiment, while JiaoHanWeissman2018L1 gives rate equivalence for multinomial distance; neither identifies the overlap-cone constant.
statements.consumer: An exact constant would calibrate polynomial degree and quantify the efficiency price of unknown observational treatment imbalance.

statements.statement:
For every even integer \(K\), let \(E_K=\inf_{p:\deg(p)\leq K}\sup_{t\in[-1,1]}\lvert\lvert tvert-p(t)vert\).  There exist symmetric probability measures \(
u_{0,K}\) and \(
u_{1,K}\) on \([-1,1]\) whose moments agree through degree \(K\) and such that \(\int\lvert tvert\,d
u_{1,K}-\int\lvert tvert\,d
u_{0,K}=2E_K\).  Moreover, there are universal constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that \(c/K\leq E_K\leq C/K\).

attestation.note: The moment-matching conclusion is taken from Lemma 1 and the order of the best absolute-value approximation error from Section 3.1; a stable arXiv handle is supplied because the used claim combines those two source locations.

statements.statement: There are positive universal constants such that, whenever \(d\geq2\), \(n\) is at least a constant multiple of \(d/\log(ed)\), and \(\log(en)\) is at most a constant multiple of \(\log(ed)\), the minimax mean-squared error for estimating \(\lVert\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\rVert_1\) from two independent samples of respective sizes \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\), one from each of \(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q\in\Delta_d\), is bounded below by a positive constant multiple of \(\min\{1,d/[n\log(en)]\}\).

source.locator: Theorem 3, equation (24), and its Poissonized lower-bound proof

attestation.note: The displayed specialization is the Poissonized unknown--unknown lower bound used from Theorem 3, equation (24), with fixed numerical constants and sample mean rescaled to 2n.

sampling_model.design: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent draws from the observed \((X,A,Y)\)-margin of \(P\).
sampling_model.units: \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with unrestricted categorical cell masses \(p_x\), including null cells.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Auxiliary Poisson thinning creates independent pilot and evaluation counts; pilot-local tensor Jackson approximation of the globally Lipschitz cell extension is lifted by centered factorial moments, clipped locally, projected globally, and Rao--Blackwellized conditional on all \(n\) observations.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper proves finite-sample upper bounds for common estimators and a minimax lower bound separated by logarithmic factors for linear treatment-specific means and the average treatment effect in the high-dimensional discrete-confounder model.
The paper constructs minimax-rate estimators for normalized two-distribution \(L_1\) distance by local polynomial approximation and proves the associated large-alphabet lower rate.
The paper pairs moment-matched priors with best approximation of absolute value and constructs asymptotically sharp estimators for a Gaussian nonsmooth functional.
The paper characterizes pathwise differentiability of the optimal value and gives online one-step inference at certain exceptional laws.
The paper obtains asymptotic inference for optimal policy values through softmax smoothing under controlled near-tie density and nuisance-rate conditions.
The paper constructs a local-moment estimator of a distribution up to permutation and proves plug-in universality for several symmetric discrete-distribution functionals.

tldr: Relative to the banked parent \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_optimal\_value\_minimax\_diagonal\_adaptive\_ratio}/\texttt{tv}\), this estimation upgrade replaces the certified \(d/n\) empirical-ratio upper bound by an explicit all-data Jackson--factorial estimator and targets a matched finite-sample risk \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\asymp_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\). A globally Lipschitz extension of the cell oracle permits one pilot-local tensor Jackson polynomial to handle null cells, off-cone pilots, unequal propensities, boundary means, and exact ties; centered factorial moments, local clipping, Poisson coupling, and Rao--Blackwellization yield the upper bound, while a dense moment-matching experiment, the exact normalized \(L_1\) slice, and padding yield the all-regime converse. The result settles uniform consistency exactly at \(d=o(n\log(en))\) and retains parametric mean-squared error exactly for bounded \(d\).

project_justification.gap: The banked parent proves a global lower envelope but certifies only \(d/n\) achievability, leaving a factor as large as a logarithm and the entire region between \(d=o(n)\) and \(d=o(n\log n)\) unresolved. Published discrete causal work treats linear targets, while published nonsmooth large-alphabet work treats normalized probability coordinates rather than observational ratios.
project_justification.niche: The oracle maximum is a degree-one homogeneous functional of four observed cell masses. Its extension to the whole orthant is globally Lipschitz, so a positive tensor Jackson convolution can adapt pointwise at the cone vertex while retaining an exponential coefficient envelope in a centered local basis.
project_justification.fill: Relative to \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_optimal\_value\_minimax\_diagonal\_adaptive\_ratio}/\texttt{tv}\), the estimation-axis delta is the named all-data estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}\) with uniform risk \(d/[n\log(ed)]\), plus a matching all-measurable-estimator lower bound and the resulting exact consistency boundary. The same assumptions and target are retained, and for every \(2\leq d<D_0\) the estimator reduces exactly to the parent's empirical-ratio estimator.

related_work: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy, \cite{ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete} [reused from parent], Introduction, Theorems 1--2, and Discussion, formulate the same structure-free categorical adjustment problem and prove a logarithmically separated minimax analysis for linear treatment-specific means; their target has no maximum or tie surface. Jiao, Han, and Weissman, \cite{JiaoHanWeissman2018L1} [reused from parent], Introduction, Theorem 3, Construction 2, Theorem 6, and Section VI, show that approximation must follow the equality diagonal for \(L_1\) distance and supply the normalized-distance lower theorem used on the exact equal-propensity slice; their unknown--unknown upper estimator does not apply to four observational masses with unknown arm denominators. Cai and Low, \cite{CaiLow2011L1} [reused from parent], Lemma 1 and Sections 3.1--4, provide the approximation--moment dual for the absolute-value cusp and the fuzzy-hypothesis template adapted in the dense lower experiment. Luedtke and van der Laan, \cite{LuedtkeVanderLaan2016OptimalValue} [reused from parent], Theorem 1 and Sections 4--7, characterize local nonregularity and online inference for the same scalar value, but do not analyze a growing unrestricted alphabet. Whitehouse, Chen, Austern, and Syrgkanis, \cite{WhitehouseChenAusternSyrgkanis2025} [reused from parent], the static-treatment theorem and controlled-density lemma, regularize the maximum by softmax; their condition permits an atom at an exact tie but restricts near ties and nuisance rates, so it does not provide a uniform result for the present class. Han, Jiao, and Weissman, \cite{HanJiaoWeissman2018Local} [new], Introduction and Sections 2--3, establish cell localization and moment reconstruction for symmetric functionals, but their quotient forgets the four-coordinate grouping needed by causal ratios. Jiao, Venkat, Han, and Weissman, \cite{JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015Functionals}, provide the earlier polynomial/factorial split-sample architecture. Wei, \cite{Wei2026OffPolicy}, gives the most recent adjacent optimal-value inference result in a trajectory experiment; its efficiency and stability theory does not subsume the present independent categorical minimax problem.
technical_internal_limitation: The estimator is explicit as a measurable Rao--Blackwellized finite-sample rule, but the conditional integration over auxiliary markings and the tensor coefficient calculation are not claimed to run in near-linear time or to be numerically stable at machine precision. The main mathematical kill test is joint: the same Jackson polynomial must satisfy both the vertex-adaptive approximation inequality and the centered coefficient envelope, and pilot-failure moments must retain the local scale \(\sqrt{p_xL_d/n}+L_d/n\).
honest_scope: The formal target is the scalar value of the unrestricted oracle policy, not regret of a learned policy and not uniform confidence intervals. Fixed overlap is maintained; vanishing overlap, growing treatment count, and sharp leading constants remain outside the theorem. Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:equal-propensity-l1-reduction}\) is only a lower-bound sanity slice. Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:parent-reduction}\) records the strict refinement: the model and estimand are identical to the parent, \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}=\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}\) only for \(2\leq d<D_0\), the matched rate implies the parent's bracket, and bounded alphabets retain minimax risk \(\Theta_\epsilon(n^{-1})\). The exact constant is exposed separately in \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp-overlap-constant}\).
